prompt: Many claim that the fast food industry had a negative impact on the environment ,eating habits and families. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
People believe that the fast food industry is a primary reason behind the ruin of eating habits, family disputes and disruption of nature. I agree with the statement that this sector has brought a lot of changes in people's life but most of them are negative.

Firstly, the most impacted part of  society by fast food outlets is youth. The food made in these restaurants lacks nutritional value because it is cooked in multiple steps before it is served to the customers to save time. Take an example of a processed junior chicken burger, it would take them less than a minute to make because of pre-cooked patties, frozen vegetables and a same cooking oil for days. On top of it, these fast food chains add a large amount of preservatives to provide longevity and to increase the shelf life of their stock. These days youngsters eat all the time from these places which leads to helath issues like diabetes, obesity and poor development of the brain and body. In a recent survey, obesity in kids surged to 140 percent since the year 1990 due to eating calorie-dense food.

Secondly, people have no choice but to eat from these restaurants because of their busy lifestyles. It is nearly impossible to raise a family with a single household income because of the increase in inflation and consumerism. Hence, both of the parents have to work to provide for their family , which results in very little or no time for cooking or to spend with their children. Due to advancements in technology, it is so easy to order food online that is delivered warm straight to their door, which is really tempting. So, they just ignore the studies and facts about the negative impact of eating junk food on their body and families.

Finally, the fast food industry needs huge amounts of packaging materials from the transportation of raw materials to the final order for their consumers. Moreover, it requires refrigeration for months to meet the surging demand from their purchasers. This whole process demands devastating amounts of energy consumption that harm nature by releasing CO2 and methane gases in the environment.

In conclusion, while fast food caters to the demands of a fast-paced lifestyle, its widespread negative impacts on individual health, family dynamics, and the environment are undeniable. Relying on processed meals daily creates lasting harm that outweighs any temporary convenience.
